subject: Proposal: Opspring hosted commit stack & rateband consolidation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@opspring.ai>, procurement@opspring.ai
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted commit proposal: step-up + consolidated rate bands

Hi Lena —

Great catching up this morning. Per our call, attached is a compact proposal that folds your current monthly hosted commit (150M gen tokens) into a stepped commit stack with a burst pocket and a single simplified rateband. High level:

• Proposed monthly commit: 450M gen tokens (3x current) with phased ramp over 90 days
• Burst pocket: 60M tokens/month for seasonal spikes (no immediate throttle)
• Soft-throttle guardrails: automatic soft-throttle at 95% of committed throughput, with a 24-hour buffer and an ops-warning channel
• Overage pricing: blended overage rate 1.6x standard per-token until monthly true-up
• SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted API endpoints; latency SLOs documented in appendix

Attachments: commit_proposal_opspring_v3.pdf (proposal + ops appendix)

Next steps we recommend:
1) Procurement review + confirmation of billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly)
2) Legal redline — we can provide a redline within 48 hours once commercial terms are confirmed
3) Ops kickoff to align burst routing and regional fallbacks

Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether Raj should be on the redline review? If that looks good I’ll loop in Karthik for the rateband and soft-throttle wording.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0112

Subject: Re: Hosted commit proposal: step-up + consolidated rate bands

Thanks Vanessa — appreciated summary. A few clarifying questions from procurement and engineering before we escalate to legal:

1) Can you confirm how the soft-throttle behaves across regions? We run failover in eu-west and want to ensure bursts routed to that region won't trigger cross-region cost surprises.
2) Is the 60M burst pocket pooled across accounts or per-tenant? We need per-product guarantees.
3) Overage billing cadence — can it be netted monthly vs billed immediately?
4) Any introductory credit available for the first two months during our ramp?

Raj and procurement are looped. If easier, happy to do a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk the redline once you confirm answers.

Best,
Lena Park
Head of Platform, Opspring
lena@opspring.ai
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Opspring proposal — internal ops/legal posture

Internal note (no external recipients) — copying Karthik for pricing/lane clarity:

Quick answers we should commit to in the customer-facing redline:
• Regions: the burst pocket is global by default but we can carve a regional allocation for EU (recommended: reserve 20% of burst to eu-west) — this avoids cross-region overage shocks.
• Burst semantics: per-tenant (product-level) allocation with an option to pool across the org for an additional fee. Ops can toggle pooling via Console.
• Overage cadence: offer monthly netting (preferred by customer) but require a 14-day invoice window for accounting.
• Intro credit: we can offer a 10% credit on the first two invoice cycles tied to adoption milestones (ramp-to-50% commit in first 30 days).

Concessions and tradeoffs: the 10% intro credit reduces first-quarter MRR but buys adoption and reduces immediate throttle risk. We should protect latency SLO language — keep the 99.9% availability but allow an exception for scheduled infra maintenance with 72-hr notice.

Action items for Karthik: please draft the updated rateband table with the blended overage multiplier (1.6x) and the EU carve option. Can you include a short alternate that has a lower overage (1.4x) if we lock a 12-month commit in year 1?

So we have internal alignment before I send the redline back to Vanessa to share with Opspring.

- Soojin
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
soojin@redwoodinference.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@opspring.ai>, Raj Singh <raj@opspring.ai>, procurement@opspring.ai
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T17:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted commit proposal: step-up + consolidated rate bands

Lena / Raj — thanks for the quick review and questions. Per internal alignment (thread below) we've updated the proposal and attached a redline that reflects the following customer-facing changes:

• Regional burst carve: Reserve 20% of the burst pocket for eu-west by default (configurable)
• Burst semantics: per-product allocation; optional org-pooling for an additional 12% fee
• Overage billing: monthly netting; 14-day invoice window for accounting; billing contact will be procurement@opspring.ai
• Introductory credit: 10% credit applied to the first two invoices, conditional on ramp milestones (50% commit utilization within 30 days)
• Alternate rate option: 1.4x overage multiplier available if Opspring signs a 12-month committed term for year 1 (details in the rateband table)
• SLA: 99.9% availability retained; scheduled maintenance exceptions with 72-hr notice retained in redline

Please review the attached redline (opspring_commit_redline_20261105.pdf). If these terms look good we can:
1) Move to a brief procurement call tomorrow to confirm billing cadence and DocuSign signatories
2) Kick off an implementation runbook for the 90-day ramp (ops + eng) — I’ll create a shared Drive folder and invite your ops lead.

Let me know preferred time for procurement call (I can do 9–11am PT or 2–4pm PT).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
